scope: Public primary-source scan for KV-cache selection, output-risk evaluation, dynamic refresh, recovery, routing, and training-free control.

unsafe_claims: StateKV is the first framework to decide what to preserve and when to refresh.
Task-conditioned routing among cache policies is the central novelty.
Dynamic attention-based cache refresh is itself novel.
Output perturbation or attention redistribution is itself novel.
verdict.defensible_delta: StateKV defines cache compression as a retained-set physical intervention at a compression-history-conditioned operating point, propagates the intervention to downstream output-distribution risk, and requires a deployable proxy to use that same retained-set risk for both action selection and stale-action regret.
verdict.remaining_risk: The exact teacher-plus-proxy-regret combination was not found in the screened public sources, but PReM, RefreshKV, QEvict, CriticalKV, ReST-KV, and LAVa make broad unification, dynamic refresh, and output-perturbation wording crowded. Novelty must be claimed at the precise state/action/risk contract level and monitored continuously.

exact_phrase_searches: KV cache refresh attention retained-set regret
KV cache selection refresh output risk
important_negative_checks: CriticalKV does not define refresh in the inspected full text.
CapKV does not define refresh in the inspected full text.
The risk of KV cache compression does not use StateKV's history-state or refresh formulation in the inspected full text.
PReM does not use StateKV's physical output-risk evaluator in the inspected full text.
QEvict does not use retained-set regret or downstream output risk in the inspected full text.

closest_work.title: PReM: Learning What to Preserve and When to Refresh for Context Compression
closest_work.overlap: Explicitly learns what evidence to preserve and when to refresh, using a dedicated memory layer and a refresh token.
closest_work.difference: Training-based learned memory; no physical retained-set intervention propagated to downstream KL risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Retire the broad preserve-and-refresh first claim.

closest_work.title: RefreshKV: Updating Small KV Cache During Long-form Generation
closest_work.overlap: Uses attention to build a small cache and query similarity to trigger full-cache refresh.
closest_work.difference: Selection and trigger are different heuristics; it retains the full cache and does not define state-conditioned downstream risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Dynamic attention refresh and query-drift triggers are prior art; compare directly.

closest_work.title: QEvict: Recoverable Quantized KV Eviction for Attention-Drift-Robust Long-Context Decoding
closest_work.overlap: Periodically reranks windows with cumulative attention and supports demotion, recovery, and promotion as importance drifts.
closest_work.difference: Three-tier window routing; no retained-set regret or downstream output-distribution risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Attention-driven dynamic recovery is not novel; QEvict is a required new baseline and discussion point.

closest_work.title: CriticalKV: Optimizing KV Cache Eviction from an Output Perturbation Perspective
closest_work.overlap: Formalizes cache eviction through attention-output perturbation and set-level deletion effects.
closest_work.difference: Local attention-output/worst-case objective; no compression-history state, downstream logit KL, or refresh objective.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Do not claim output perturbation as new; emphasize history-conditioned downstream physical risk.

closest_work.title: ReST-KV: Robust KV Cache Eviction with Layer-wise Output Reconstruction and Spatial-Temporal Smoothing
closest_work.overlap: Optimizes layer-wise output reconstruction while accounting for attention redistribution and temporal dynamics.
closest_work.difference: Layer-local reconstruction and smoothing rather than downstream state-conditioned output risk and same-risk refresh regret.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Ablate against layer-output reconstruction and avoid generic redistribution claims.

closest_work.title: LAVa: Layer-wise KV Cache Eviction with Dynamic Budget Allocation
closest_work.overlap: Uses layer-wise output information loss and dynamic budgets in a training-free eviction framework.
closest_work.difference: No compression-history-conditioned retained-set risk or refresh regret.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Do not market a generic unified information-loss framework.

closest_work.title: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction via a Unified Information-Theoretic Objective
closest_work.overlap: Provides a unified mutual-information/log-determinant selection objective and leverage approximation.
closest_work.difference: Linear-Gaussian capacity objective; no history state or refresh.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Distinguish output risk from information capacity.

closest_work.title: The risk of KV cache compression
closest_work.overlap: Characterizes minimax risk and intrinsic compressibility of KV caches.
closest_work.difference: Population/minimax compression risk rather than a trajectory-local physical action risk used by a controller.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Define the two meanings of risk explicitly in title, abstract, and related work.

closest_work.title: Minimal-Intervention KV Retention via Set-Conditioned Diversity
closest_work.overlap: Optimizes retained sets jointly through diversity/facility-location structure.
closest_work.difference: Value-space coverage rather than physical downstream risk at a history-conditioned state.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Set-level selection alone is not a novelty claim.

closest_work.title: PolyKV: Heterogeneous Retention and Allocation for KV Cache Compression
closest_work.overlap: Routes layers to different compression policies and allocates budgets.
closest_work.difference: Layer-wise method portfolio rather than one risk-consistent action proxy.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Demote a cache-method router to baseline/diagnostic, not core contribution.

closest_work.title: DynamicKV: Task-Aware Adaptive KV Cache Compression
closest_work.overlap: Task-aware dynamic budget allocation with periodic updates.
closest_work.difference: Task/layer allocation rather than physical state-conditioned downstream risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: The previously planned task-conditioned router is crowded and should be abandoned as the main route.

closest_work.title: Task-KV: Task-aware KV Cache Optimization via Semantic Differentiation of Attention Heads
closest_work.overlap: Uses task-aware semantic head differentiation for cache optimization.
closest_work.difference: Head/task allocation rather than state/action/risk control.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Prompt/task metadata routing is not a clean novelty axis.

closest_work.title: MemDecay: Region-Aware KV Cache Eviction for Efficient LLM Agent Inference
closest_work.overlap: Training-free region priorities, decay, and attention-based score refresh.
closest_work.difference: Semantic-region heuristic rather than teacher-aligned physical action risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Do not rely on prompt-region metadata as the main novel controller.

closest_work.title: CONF-KV: Confidence-Aware KV Cache Eviction with Mixed-Precision Storage for Long-Horizon LLM
closest_work.overlap: Uses next-token uncertainty to change per-step cache budget and attention/recency for selection.
closest_work.difference: Confidence controls budget, not retained-set physical risk or regret.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Output entropy alone is not a new state-conditioned controller.

closest_work.title: Expected Attention: KV Cache Compression by Estimating Attention from Future Queries Distribution
closest_work.overlap: Training-free estimation of future attention for cache retention.
closest_work.difference: Future-query attention utility rather than history-conditioned downstream output risk.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Future-attention prediction must be treated as a baseline proxy family.

closest_work.title: Make Each Token Count: Towards Improving Long-Context Performance with KV Cache Eviction
closest_work.overlap: Learns token retention for global future utility.
closest_work.difference: Training-based gates rather than training-free physical-risk alignment.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Use as the trained future-utility contrast.

closest_work.title: The Pitfalls of KV Cache Compression
closest_work.overlap: Shows instruction loss and leakage that standard compression evaluations miss.
closest_work.difference: Evaluation/failure analysis rather than StateKV's method.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Add multi-instruction and system-prompt robustness before broad deployment claims.

closest_work.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
closest_work.overlap: Reconstructs omitted numerator and denominator attention mass with a residual cache and dynamic gate.
closest_work.difference: Storage/action reconstruction mechanism rather than history-conditioned teacher risk and same-risk regret.
closest_work.novelty_implication: Nearest-value merge and residual reconstruction are now crowded auxiliary mechanisms, not the central claim.
